video_title: Amy Oldenburg: We Might Not Need Blockchain to Solve Everything
gist: Amy, who leads Morgan Stanley's firm-wide digital asset strategy, says the bank now has live digital asset activity in all three divisions, including its first DTCC tokenized equity and treasury trades, but argues tokenization is only step one: the payoff needs a digital cash leg (stablecoins, tokenized deposits, tokenized MMFs), T0/24/7 markets and programmability, and blockchain may not be needed for every efficiency gain. She flags DeFi auto-liquidation and AML/KYC as bank hurdles, sees multi-asset and income crypto products and new lending models as next, and warns AI agents will sharply raise market velocity.

themes.theme: Morgan Stanley's firm-wide digital asset rollout

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley created a firm-wide digital asset strategy seat in January and now has digital asset activity live in all three divisions: institutional securities, wealth and investment management.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: A top-tier bank treating digital assets as a cross-divisional business line signals institutional adoption is moving from pilots to production.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley completed its first DTCC tokenized equity trade and tokenized treasury trade in its institutional securities business, with the tokenized equity trade settled through its Trajectory Cross ATS.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Live production trades by DTCC participants mark tokenized settlement crossing into core market plumbing; watch DTCC tokenization pilots and participating venues.
insights.quote: we celebrated the first DTCC tokenized equity trade and tokenized treasury trade

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley's wealth arm has broadened crypto ETP and private offerings and added spot crypto trading on E-Trade, while its investment management arm has launched ETPs.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Wirehouse distribution of spot crypto and in-house ETPs widens the retail/wealth funnel for crypto assets and pressures competing brokers.

insights.claim: Tokenized equities on Morgan Stanley's trading venue are targeted for early 2027.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: A dated milestone to track for tokenized equity market structure and volumes on bank-run ATSs.

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley launched a Digital Asset Lab in September primarily to test blockchains, wallet models, vault constructs and smart contracts safely before production, with building proprietary tools a longer-term option where nothing suitable exists to buy.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Signals a buy-first stance near term, implying vendor opportunities for custody, wallet and smart-contract infrastructure providers.
insights.quote: We don't want to be learning in production

insights.claim: Amy argues that Morgan Stanley's cybersecurity, tech-risk and resiliency infrastructure is an underappreciated competitive edge in digital assets, including in moving spot crypto in kind into ETPs.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Security and custody credibility may be the incumbents' moat versus crypto-native platforms in winning wealth-client crypto flows.

themes.theme: Bank strategy follows existing revenue pools

insights.claim: Banks will pursue blockchain where their own revenue is concentrated: Morgan Stanley, lacking a big consumer branch network, prioritizes equities and wealth over payments, while consumer-heavy G-SIBs lead on stablecoin payments.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Map each bank's tokenization bets to its fee pools to predict who leads where (payments vs. equities vs. wealth).

insights.claim: Reducing settlement friction (e.g., T0, no money in flight) benefits clients but erodes some industry revenue lines, forcing banks into a defensive response plus a growth push into new business models such as new lending models.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Float- and friction-based revenues at incumbents are at risk; look for which firms replace them with collateral/lending and 'earn' products.
insights.quote: sometimes that reducing the friction like is not great for some of the industry's areas where they make the revenue

insights.claim: If regulators allowed it, the first product Amy would push is new lending models, such as using assets previously ineligible as collateral.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Regulatory changes on collateral eligibility of digital/tokenized assets are a key catalyst for bank crypto revenue.

themes.theme: Tokenization: rails first, redesign and programmability later

insights.claim: Tokenizing assets is only step one; the real value comes later from redesigning workflows like corporate actions and enabling smart-contract programmability, which requires assets to move in real time.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Value accrues in a second phase; early tokenization volume is a leading indicator, not the payoff.
insights.quote: Tokenizing assets in some ways is not the hard part.

insights.claim: Amy compares the current tokenization phase to late-1990s corporate websites that were mere landing pages before smartphones and app stores unlocked real functionality.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Expect a long build-out with today's use cases looking primitive relative to eventual applications.

insights.claim: Blockchain is mainly putting a magnifying glass on operational workflows; many efficiency gains may come from off-chain or centralized ledgers rather than decentralized chains.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Don't assume public-chain token value capture from bank tokenization; some efficiency may be captured by private/centralized ledgers.
insights.quote: we might not need blockchain to solve for everything

insights.claim: Equity markets are already extremely efficient thanks to low-latency electronic trading, so blockchain's value there lies more in collateral efficiency than execution speed.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of tokenized-equity pitches built on execution efficiency; focus on collateral mobility.

insights.claim: US markets are moving to 23.5-hour trading in December as a step toward 24/7, and after decades of compression from T5 to T1 settlement, T0 is the logical next step.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Extended hours and T0 change liquidity, margin and funding dynamics; infrastructure and data providers benefit.
insights.quote: We're moving to 23.5 trading in December.

insights.claim: Running legacy and tokenized assets side by side while still delivering a unified client experience will be one of the hardest challenges for a long time.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Transition costs will be prolonged; firms with unified multi-asset platforms gain an edge.

insights.claim: Amy's top infrastructure priority is unifying separate equities, fixed income and private-markets systems into one multi-asset platform.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Large bank tech spend is shifting toward platform unification, a tailwind for vendors enabling multi-asset ledgers.

themes.theme: Digital cash leg: stablecoins, tokenized deposits and tokenized MMFs

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley's tokenized secondary for Figure was constrained because its broker-dealer could not use stablecoins to settle the cash leg; any tokenized asset class needs a digital cash leg to capture shorter settlement benefits.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: The cash leg is the bottleneck for tokenized markets scale; watch broker-dealer stablecoin/tokenized deposit settlement permissions.
insights.quote: our broker dealer was not able to use stable coins to settle the trade

insights.claim: Morgan Stanley is building stablecoin support not only for payments but also for utility functions needed to settle trades.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Bank adoption of stablecoins for settlement expands institutional demand for regulated stablecoins.

insights.claim: Stablecoins and tokenized deposits are optimized for different use cases and today's versions are early; tokenized money market funds are an adjacent instrument enabling real-time yield and intraday exposure.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Expect multiple digital cash instruments to coexist; tokenized MMF issuers are positioned for programmable collateral demand.

insights.claim: Banks need not rely on DeFi for yield on idle cash: tokenized money market funds can be sold and used same-day, removing T+1 and market-cutoff delays that can turn a Thursday cash need into a Monday availability.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Tokenized MMFs are a bank-native answer to the stablecoin yield debate and could retain deposits on platform.
insights.quote: I don't need D Fi to solve that

insights.claim: Amy declined to pick stablecoins vs. tokenized deposits for 2028 but expects tokenized deposits within institutions and stablecoins driving global payments and dollar access, especially in emerging markets.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: EM demand for dollar access is a structural driver of stablecoin growth.

insights.claim: Banks' main hurdles to using DeFi are AML/KYC and jurisdictional controls, likely solved first through walled-garden or whitelisted models.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Permissioned DeFi pools are the likely first bridge to TradFi; watch protocols offering whitelisted versions.

insights.claim: DeFi auto-liquidations clear market stress far faster than traditional markets, where deleveraging can take weeks, but are incompatible with wealth relationship management, requiring backup collateral or secondary structures.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Bank-integrated DeFi lending will need modified liquidation mechanics; protocols adapting first can capture TradFi flows.
insights.quote: I don't believe that auto liquidating assets of our clients are going to be very good for relationship management

themes.theme: Next-gen crypto products and AI-driven market velocity

insights.claim: Amy is surprised multi-asset crypto products haven't grown more, since tracking separate Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Near and Hyperliquid positions is hard for wealth clients when crypto is a small slice of the portfolio.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Diversified crypto index ETPs are an underserved wealth-channel opportunity.
insights.quote: my Bitcoin exposure my Ethereum my Solana my Near, my Hyperliquid

insights.claim: Beyond passive single-asset ETFs, Amy expects more crypto products offering downside protection and income streams, citing recent filings in that direction.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Watch for buffered and income crypto ETP launches as next product wave.

insights.claim: AI agents will sharply increase transaction activity and velocity, so infrastructure must handle real-time data and throughput; a Silicon Valley Bank-style run with stablecoins and agents instead of wires would move far faster.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Bank-run and meme-event dynamics could accelerate dramatically; favor infrastructure/throughput plays and stress-test liquidity assumptions.
insights.quote: what would Silicon Valley Bank look like if you had stable coins and do digital cash movements

insights.claim: AI is democratizing quant and high-frequency trading to retail globally, and much DeFi volume comes from outside the US, driven by a trader mentality.
insights.speaker: Amy Oldenburg (Morgan Stanley)
insights.so_what: Non-US retail-driven on-chain volume is a growth driver for DeFi venues and trading infrastructure.
